label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Handover for Thursday's launch (DRAFT, not yet shared)

DRAFT. Marieke to read before sharing.

Inês,

My father is ill and I am with my family, so I am taking the train tonight and I don't know how long I will be away. That means you are doing Thursday's launch without me, and I found an error in figure 3 only this afternoon, so I am leaving you a mess as well. I'm sorry. It's the worst possible timing, and the mistake is mine, not yours.

I also want to say something plainly. I trust you completely with this. You know the paper as well as I do, you ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself, and I would rather have you in that room than anyone else, me included. I mean that.

Below is what happened, what needs doing and in which order, and what I would say if I were standing there.

WHAT WENT WRONG

Figure 3 and the summary used the 2030 revenue estimate from an old run, one where the free allocation phase-out was not applied. The correct 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion.

- PDF v7 on the drive is corrected (pages 3, 14 and 15). Use that one.
- Deck v4 is not corrected yet: slides 6 and 9 (slide 9 is the revenue chart).
- The embargoed press release Hanna sent on Friday still says 2.1. It went to our 34 Brussels contacts, and the embargo lifts Thursday at 10:00.

The conclusion of the paper does not change. Only the headline number does. That is the line to hold on to.

WHAT TO DO, IN ORDER

1. Tuesday morning, first thing: Hanna and the press release.
Hanna may not know about the error yet, so please speak to her before anything else. The journalists have the wrong number, and it needs to be corrected before the embargo lifts on Thursday at 10:00. Ideally it goes out on Tuesday, so that the two journalists she has booked for Wednesday already have the right figure when we talk to them. It should go to the same 34 contacts, clearly marked as a correction, with 1.4 billion and a line saying the conclusions are unchanged. Hanna knows how to word this better than I do, so it's her call. If she needs a senior name on it, Geert knows I am away and can sign off the corrected release. Just ask him.

2. Tuesday: fix the deck.
Slides 6 and 9 need the new number. Please also search the whole deck and my speaker notes for "2.1" in case it appears anywhere else. While you are in there, the presentation is now 15 minutes, not 20 (see point 3), so it needs trimming. You know the deck better than I do, since you shortened it to 14 slides, so cut whatever you would cut. Also check that anything going online or printed for Thursday is PDF v7 and not an older version.

3. Tuesday: Tomás and the changed timings.
Tomás wrote on Monday that the MEP has a vote moved into Thursday lunchtime and has to leave at 13:30. He asked for:
- the presentation at 15 minutes instead of 20
- the panel to start at 12:50
- room for at least two questions from her before she goes

The run of show on the drive still has the old times, so it needs updating. His email doesn't say what happens to the rest of the afternoon, so please ask him two things: where her two questions fit, and who moderates after she leaves. As far as I can tell the Q&A stays at 13:40 and the close at 14:00, but check with him rather than trusting my guess. The welcome stays at 12:30 and the presentation at 12:35.

4. Tuesday: tell Abena and Florian Kessler about the correction.
I would send both of them PDF v7 with two lines saying the 2030 figure has been corrected from 2.1 to 1.4 billion and that the conclusions stand. Abena should hear it from us and not discover it on Thursday. Kessler is going to raise things on the panel, and I would rather he has heard it from us than score a point with it. You decide how to phrase it. It doesn't need an apology beyond a plain "we found an error in our own run and corrected it."

5. Wednesday by 12:00: badges.
Tomás needs the final names of everyone from our side by Wednesday 12:00. After that security will not let anyone in. Please make the list (you, Hanna, anyone else coming) and send it to him well before noon. Take me off it.

6. Wednesday 14:00 and 15:00: the two press calls.
Hanna booked these for me: 20 minutes each, by phone, a trade newsletter and a Belgian daily. They are in the calendar and she is confirming them. Please take them, unless Hanna and you agree it should be someone else. They are a good chance to give the corrected figure directly, and to say clearly what changed and what didn't.

7. Wednesday: test Abena's remote link.
She tested it on the 18th and it worked, and the link is in the calendar invite. The room is in the Parliament, though, so I would ask her for a quick re-test with Tomás's people if they allow it. I'm not worried, but I would rather we found out on Wednesday.

8. Thursday.
- 10:00: embargo lifts.
- By 12:00: guests at the security entrance. Tomás collects the badges. A light lunch is outside the room from 12:00.
- 12:30: Lindqvist welcomes.
- 12:35: your presentation, 15 minutes.
- 12:50: panel with Abena (remote), Florian Kessler and you, moderated by Lindqvist.
- 13:30: Lindqvist has to leave.
- Q&A and close: see point 3 for the times to confirm.

9. After the event.
Lucy Tran from the Halvorsen Foundation is coming with a colleague. For their grant report they need two photos from the event and the attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December. Please ask someone to take the photos on the day and count heads at the door.

IF ANYONE ASKS ABOUT THE 2.1

It was my mistake and you should say so. Something like: "There was an error in one of our model runs, which Marieke found and corrected. The 2030 figure is 1.4 billion, not 2.1, and the conclusions of the paper are unchanged." Say it once, calmly, and move on. Please don't take any of it on yourself.

KESSLER AND THE 80%

He has told us what he is going to raise: the 80% pass-through assumption in section 4, and resource shuffling. I expect he will try to make the whole afternoon about the 80%, and you shouldn't let him set the tone. My notes for you:

- Pass-through: 80% is the central case, but annex B runs 40% and 60%. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. You ran those runs, so you can say exactly that, openly, without getting defensive. Admitting where it weakens makes us more credible, not less.
- Resource shuffling: we agree it is a real risk. It is in section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission's monitoring report.

Give him a straight answer, then bring it back to what the paper is about, which is what the border revenues mean for the least developed countries. That is also where Abena comes in. She was strong on the call and will probably back us on the LDC side, so let her.

ON THE DAY

You are better live than you think. In Lisbon, when the projector died at the COP side event, you rescued my panel without any fuss. If something goes wrong in the room on Thursday, you will do the same. You don't need to perform. You need to be clear, honest about the numbers, and yourself.

REACHING ME

You can call me, but after 9 tomorrow (Tuesday) I might not pick up. If it can wait, send a message and I will answer when I can. If it can't wait, still try, but please don't hold anything up on my account. Make the call yourself. I will back whatever you decide, and Geert is there if you need a senior voice.

Thank you, and sorry again for leaving it like this. You will be great on Thursday.

Marieke
